samples.summary: Parquet import materializes an unbounded number of rows — the MAX_IMPORT_CELLS budget the CSV path uses is not applied, and `truncated`/`rowCount` are never reported
samples.evidence: `importParquet` calls `importParquetFile` → `importRecordsAsSheet`, which writes every record with no cell budget, unlike `importCsv` (`parseCsvFile` → `createTableWriter`, capped by `MAX_IMPORT_CELLS = 40_000` in packages/sheets/src/import/csv-importer.ts:155). Parquet is a compressed columnar bulk format, so a few-MB file routinely holds hundreds of thousands of rows; the resulting document exceeds the Yorkie materialize limit the cap exists to protect (docs/design/sheets/file-import.md Current Limitations #2: 'Import is capped by the Yorkie materialize limit'). The existing cap helper was available for reuse. Note the todo defers the cap+Connect routing to FI-5, so this may be intentionally out of scope.

samples.summary: manualChunks folds hyparquet/fzstd/hysnappy into the always-loaded `sheet-core` chunk, defeating the dynamic import in the Parquet importer
samples.evidence: parquet-importer.ts deliberately `await import('hyparquet')`/`import('hyparquet-compressors')` so the decoder and its zstd/snappy codecs load only on a Parquet import, but vite.config.ts:183-189 assigns those modules to `sheet-core` — the same chunk as packages/sheets/src/{view,model,store} (line 202-208), which every spreadsheet viewer loads. Result: all sheet users download the Parquet reader and codecs even though they never import a Parquet file. A dedicated `sheet-parquet` chunk would keep the lazy intent (the stated motivation was avoiding one chunk per dynamic import, which a single named chunk also achieves).

finding.summary: Parquet import materializes an unbounded number of rows — the MAX_IMPORT_CELLS budget the CSV path uses is not applied, and `truncated`/`rowCount` are never reported
finding.evidence: `importParquet` calls `importParquetFile` → `importRecordsAsSheet`, which writes every record with no cell budget, unlike `importCsv` (`parseCsvFile` → `createTableWriter`, capped by `MAX_IMPORT_CELLS = 40_000` in packages/sheets/src/import/csv-importer.ts:155). Parquet is a compressed columnar bulk format, so a few-MB file routinely holds hundreds of thousands of rows; the resulting document exceeds the Yorkie materialize limit the cap exists to protect (docs/design/sheets/file-import.md Current Limitations #2: 'Import is capped by the Yorkie materialize limit'). verdict.reason: The factual absence is real — the Parquet path (parquet-importer.ts:11-27 -> record-importer.ts:35-83) applies no cell budget and importParquet (sheet-import-actions.ts:118-127) reports no truncated/rowCount, while MAX_IMPORT_CELLS (csv-importer.ts:155) is used only by the CSV writer, and the only upstream guard is the generic 50 MB upload cap (file-meta.ts:22). But it is not blocking under the design-fit rubric. (1) The cap is explicitly a different subissue: the todo assigns "Materialize cap + Connect suggestion" to FI-5 (depends on FI-4) at todo:128-138, while FI-2's shipped item is scoped to "Small local: client-side hyparquet … a small Parquet imports with no server round-trip" (todo:60-63), with the large path an unchecked DuckDB item (todo:64-69). (2) The design doc puts the materialize cap in the backend/large-file path (file-import.md:111-112, Rollout Phase 3 at 164-165, Risks at 173); §2 for the client-side CSV path (85-96) imposes no cap requirement, so no documented rule obliges client-side small-file importers to carry one. (3) The uncapped shape is the repo's existing documented pattern for whole-file client importers, not a divergence Parquet introduces: JSON uses the same uncapped importRecordsAsSheet (json-importer.ts:96), XLSX reads whole, and sheet-import-actions.ts:17-24 and 100-107 state the rule explicitly ("Only the CSV path can report these — the XLSX and JSON importers read their input whole and have no budget to stop on"). Under this lens the best characterization is "reuse available but not required" / "divergence from the documented shape that still behaves as specified" — both graded minor, which never blocks. The unbounded-materialization risk itself belongs to the correctness lens, not spec-conformance.
